purpose: Redirects (302) to the Grafana dbdome dashboard at http://<request-host>:3000/d/ad7kkx7/dbdome; logs the request, no DB work.

Renders an inline HTML form: the /addrecipients variant shows a recipient-group form (POST /submit-addrecipients); the /mailconfiguration variant shows an SMTP mail-config form, prefilling smtp_* fields and recipients from config.mail_config and config.mail_groups (password via decrypt_secret) when row_id is supplied.
Serves the alert dashboard screen (renders templates/alert_dashboard.html).
Serves the alert rules screen (renders templates/alert_rules.html).
Serves the alert thresholds screen (renders templates/alert_thresholds.html).
Returns all configured recurring access-review cycles from config.access_review_cycles (ordered by cycle_id) - the campaign definitions: name, reviewer, frequency, regulation scope and next due date.

Creates a new recurring access-review cycle in config.access_review_cycles from JSON body cycle_name (required), reviewer_email (required), frequency (default QUARTERLY), regulation and next_cycle_due_at; returns the new cycle_id.

Lists open access-review campaign instances (status OPEN or IN_PROGRESS) from log.access_review_instances joined to config.access_review_cycles, showing cycle name, scope regulations, reviewer email and the review period, ordered by soonest due date (up to 200) - the reviewer's outstanding worklist.

Lists alert rules from config.alerts_issue_root_causes (air) left-joined to config.alerts (alert_name) and to config.webook_alerts where row_id=1 for send_mail/send_siem/send_diagnosis flags (defaulting false), ordered by issue_id then rootcause_number; also returns distinct issues (issue_id, name) from rootcause.issues and all alerts (row_id, alert_name) from config.alerts. Responds with JSON {rules, issues, alerts} or a 500 with empty lists on error.

Lists alert thresholds by joining config.alerts_thresholds to config.alerts and config.thresholds (selecting row_id, alert_name, level, value_start, value_end, alert_id, threshold_id) ordered by alert_name, casting value_start/value_end to float (0 if null), plus a list of all alerts (row_id, alert_name) from config.alerts; returns JSON {thresholds, alerts} or a 500 with empty lists on error.

Returns JSON for the security alert dashboard: runs ALERT_DASHBOARD_SQL against alerts.mail_alert_log (mal) filtered to the last `days` (default 7), optionally adding `AND mal.server=%s` when `server` is given and Python-filtering rows by `severity` when supplied, ordered by entry_date DESC; computes severity counts (critical/high/medium) and distinct server/root_cause tallies, queries DISTINCT servers from alerts.mail_alert_log over the last 90 days, and responds with stats, servers, and a hierarchical tree from build_alert_tree(rows); on error returns a 500 with empty stats/servers and an empty SEC domain tree.

Paginated firewall audit log query over log.firewall_audit_log left-joined to config.firewall_policies (policy_name via matched_policy); accepts page (default 1), page_size (default 50) and optional filters action (exact), server_name and db_user (ILIKE substring), and from_dt/to_dt event_time bounds; returns total count plus rows (event_id, event_time ISO, server_name, vendor, db_user, client_ip, db_name, action_taken, policy_name, regulation, risk_score, sql_statement truncated to 200 chars) ordered by event_time DESC with LIMIT/OFFSET. On error it calls db_write_log and returns a 500 with total 0 and empty rows.

Returns JSON {"reports": [...]} listing generated PDF files (newest first) in the BASE_DIR/reports/compliance directory; for each file it infers the regulation (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR or SOC2, else UNKNOWN) from the filename and reports filename, generated_at (mtime), and size_kb; returns 500 with empty list on error.

Serves a compliance PDF for download; takes the path filename, reduces it to its basename, and returns a FileResponse (media type application/pdf) from BASE_DIR/reports/compliance, raising HTTP 404 if the file does not exist.

POST handler that reads JSON body {regulation, lookback_days (default 7), recipients}, validates regulation is one of PCI-DSS/HIPAA/GDPR/SOC2 (else 400), then calls processes.compliance_report_generator.run_compliance_report_on_demand to generate the PDF on demand, logs the result, and returns {message, filename}; returns 500 with detail on error.

Returns JSON {"schedules": [...]} selecting schedule_id, regulation, frequency, is_active, recipients and last_run_at (ISO-formatted) from config.compliance_report_schedules ordered by regulation; logs via db_write_log and returns 500 with empty list on error.

PUT handler that updates a row in config.compliance_report_schedules identified by path schedule_id; reads a JSON body and dynamically sets only the provided is_active, recipients and/or frequency fields, commits, and returns {"message": "Schedule updated"}; returns 400 if no updatable fields are supplied and rolls back with 500 on error.

Returns up to 500 DDL audit records from log.ddl_audit_log (event_time, server_name, db_user, ddl_command, object_name, ddl_statement, risk_level, regulation) ordered by event_time DESC, optionally filtered by the ddl_command, risk_level, and regulation query params; returns JSON {rows} with ISO-formatted timestamps or {error, rows: []} with HTTP 500 on failure.

Returns a 30-day DDL audit summary from log.ddl_audit_log grouped by event date and server_name with total_events, destructive_events (DROP/TRUNCATE) and high_risk_events (risk_level='HIGH') counts, ordered by date and total descending and limited to 200 rows, as JSON {rows}; returns {error, rows: []} with HTTP 500 on failure.
POST that reads JSON body row_id and deletes the matching config.alerts_issue_root_causes row, commits, and returns {message:'Deleted'}; returns a 500 with the exception message on error.
POST that reads JSON body key, deletes the matching row from config.global_params, commits, and returns {message:'Deleted'}; returns a 500 with the exception message on error.

POST that reads JSON body row_id, looks up the linked threshold_id in config.alerts_thresholds, deletes the config.alerts_thresholds row and then the corresponding config.thresholds row (if found), commits, and returns {message:'Deleted'}; on error rolls back and returns a 500 with the exception message.
POST that reads JSON body row_id and deletes the matching config.webook_alerts row, commits, and returns {message:'Deleted'}; returns a 500 with the exception message on error.

Returns up to 500 PENDING PII discovery candidates from log.discovery_candidates (candidate_id, server_name, db_name, table_schema, table_name, column_name, data_type, pii_type, detection_method, confidence_score, sample_matches, review_status, discovered_at) ordered by confidence_score then discovered_at descending, as JSON {rows} with ISO-formatted timestamps; returns {error, rows: []} with HTTP 500 on failure.

Updates the review_status of a single log.discovery_candidates row identified by candidate_id (path param) to the review_status from the JSON body (default 'DISMISSED'), commits, and returns {message: 'Candidate <status>'}; rolls back and returns {detail} with HTTP 500 on failure.

Builds the Grafana panel PDF via _build_panel_pdf from POSTed form fields and emails it as an attachment to the parsed recipients (split on commas/semicolons) using SMTP settings loaded from config.mail_config via _load_mail_config and _send_pdf_email; logs the send with db_write_log and returns an HTML confirmation page, or raises HTTP 400/404/500 (500 if mail_config has no rows).

Renders a small self-contained HTML dialog prompting for email recipients, subject (defaulting to 'DBDOME report: <panel title>' resolved via _lookup_panel_sql), and an optional message; requires dashboard and panel query params and re-emits all incoming query params as hidden inputs so the form POSTs everything to /api/email-panel.

Lists the 100 most recent compliance evidence packages from log.evidence_packages (newest first): package name, regulation, reporting period, generator, status, file size, SHA-256 hashes of the PDF/CSV artefacts and their stored paths - the audit-evidence archive index.

Starts asynchronous generation of a compliance evidence package: parses period_start/period_end and launches processes.evidence_package_generator.generate_evidence_package on a background daemon thread for the given regulation (generated_by defaults to 'ui-user'), returning immediately while the package builds.

Downloads a completed evidence package artefact: looks up pdf_path/csv_zip_path/status in log.evidence_packages; file_type 'txt' streams the report file (text/plain) and 'zip' streams the CSV archive (application/zip). Returns 404 if the package/file is missing, 409 if status is not COMPLETE, and 400 for an invalid file_type.

Lists firewall policies from config.firewall_policies (policy_id, policy_name, vendor, action, condition_type, condition_value, severity, regulation, priority, is_active, created_at, updated_at), ordered by priority then policy_id; optional query filters action, regulation, and is_active (string compared case-insensitively to 'true'). Returns JSON {policies:[...]} with timestamps ISO-formatted, or 500 {error, policies:[]} on failure.

Inserts a new row into config.firewall_policies from the JSON body (requires policy_name; defaults vendor='all', action='ALERT', condition_type='query_pattern', condition_value='', priority=100, is_active=True, regulation=None, severity='MEDIUM'), commits, then calls reload_policy_cache() from processes.firewall_policy_engine to refresh the live cache. Returns {message, policy_id} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Seeds default firewall policies for a regulation given in the JSON body (must be one of PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, SOC2, else 400) by inserting hardcoded template rows into config.firewall_policies with vendor='all' and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, counting rows actually added, then calls reload_policy_cache(). Returns {message, added} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Deletes the config.firewall_policies row matching the path policy_id, commits, and calls reload_policy_cache() from processes.firewall_policy_engine to refresh the live cache. Returns {message:'Policy deleted'} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Updates config.firewall_policies for the given policy_id, dynamically setting only supplied body keys (policy_name, vendor, action, condition_type, condition_value, priority, is_active, regulation, severity) plus updated_at=NOW(); returns 400 if no updatable fields. On commit it calls reload_policy_cache() to refresh the engine cache. Returns {message} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Returns a fleet overview of database servers by running FLEET_SQL with a days window (default 7); aggregates stats (total, active, inactive, distinct vendors, servers with alerts, total alerts) plus a sorted vendor list and the per-server rows as JSON, returning zeroed stats with HTTP 500 on error.
Returns all rows from config.global_params (key, value) ordered by key as JSON {params:[{key,value}]}; on error returns a 500 with an empty params list.
Returns all GRC alert channels by selecting every row from config.grc_alert_channels ordered by channel_id, as JSON {"channels": [...]}; on error returns 500 with {"error", "channels": []}.

Creates a GRC alert channel by INSERTing into config.grc_alert_channels (channel_name defaulting to channel_type, channel_type, min_severity default 'MEDIUM', regulations and feature_sources default empty lists, and JSON config default {}) from the request JSON, and returns the new channel_id; rolls back and returns 500 on error.
Deletes the config.grc_alert_channels row matching the path channel_id and returns {"message": "Channel deleted"}; rolls back and returns 500 on error.

Updates the config.grc_alert_channels row for the path channel_id, dynamically setting only the provided fields among channel_name, channel_type, min_severity, regulations, feature_sources, is_active and JSON config; returns 400 if no fields are supplied and rolls back with 500 on error.

Returns the 200 most recent GRC alert delivery records (sent_at, channel_type, source_feature, severity, server_name, event_summary, success, error_message) from log.grc_alert_delivery_log ordered by sent_at descending, with sent_at ISO-formatted, as {"rows": [...]}.

Deletes an SMTP mail configuration by calling the config.delete_mail_config(p_row_id, p_force) stored procedure with row_id and a force flag (default False) taken from the JSON body; returns {ok: true} on success or {ok: false, error} with HTTP 400 on failure.

Returns all SMTP configs from config.mail_config (row_id, smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_user, tls, mail_sender) and all recipient groups from config.mail_groups (row_id, mail_config_id, group_name, recipients, is_active), each ordered by row_id, as JSON {configs, groups}; returns {ok: false, error} with HTTP 400 on failure.

Deletes a mail recipient group by calling the config.delete_mail_group(p_row_id) stored procedure with row_id from the JSON body; returns {ok: true} on success or {ok: false, error} with HTTP 400 on failure.

Lists data-masking rules from config.masking_rules with optional filters (pii_type, mask_type, is_active, case-insensitive server_name). Each rule shows the target server/database/table/column, pii_type, mask_type, allowed_roles, regulation and active flag - the masking policy set.

Upserts a masking rule into config.masking_rules (ON CONFLICT on server+table+column) from JSON server_name/table_name/column_name (required) plus pii_type (default GENERIC), mask_type (default HASH), allowed_roles[] and regulation; returns rule_id. Then reloads the data-masking engine's rule cache so masking applies immediately.

Triggers an immediate sync: runs data_masking_engine.sync_masking_rules() to regenerate masking rules from the confirmed monitoring.sensitive_schema inventory and reload them, keeping masking coverage aligned with newly discovered PII.

Updates a masking rule: patches any of pii_type/mask_type/allowed_roles/regulation/is_active/server_name/table_name/column_name/database_name on config.masking_rules (bumps updated_at) and reloads the masking engine's rule cache.

Lists firewall/access policy exception requests from config.policy_exceptions (up to 200, newest first). Filters by approval_status when status is supplied, otherwise returns only PENDING and APPROVED. Each row shows the target policy/server/db_user/CIDR, requester, approver, business justification and expiry - the exception approval queue.

Submits a new policy-exception request into config.policy_exceptions from JSON body policy_id (required), server_name, db_user, client_ip_cidr, expires_at (required), business_justification (required) and requested_by; status defaults to PENDING. Returns the new exception_id.

Approves or edits a policy exception: patches approval_status, approved_by, expires_at and/or business_justification on config.policy_exceptions for exception_id. When approval_status becomes APPROVED it reloads the firewall policy cache (processes.firewall_policy_engine.reload_policy_cache) so the exception takes effect immediately.

Generates and streams a PDF of a Grafana table panel via _build_panel_pdf using required query params dashboard (uid) and panel (id), treating all other query params (except from/to) as Grafana template variable values; returns the PDF as a FileResponse, or raises HTTP 400/404/500 (logging failures via db_write_log).

Returns up to 500 recent privilege-change (GRANT/REVOKE) audit records from log.privilege_change_log, newest first, optionally filtered by operation and mapped regulation. Each row shows grantor, grantee, privilege_type, object_name and whether it carried WITH GRANT / admin option - the DCL change audit trail.

Aggregates the last 7 days of GRANT events from log.privilege_change_log by server and grantee, returning grant_count, admin_option_count (grants carrying WITH GRANT) and last_event, top 100 by grant volume - a 'who received the most privileges lately' summary card.

Returns JSON {"rows": [...]} from config.regulation_controls (control_id, regulation, clause_number, control_name, control_type, policy_ids, feature_refs) with a computed coverage_status of COVERED or GAP based on whether policy_ids/feature_refs are populated; filters by optional regulation query param in SQL and by optional status query param in Python, ordered by regulation and clause_number; returns 500 with empty list on error.

Returns JSON {"reports": [...], "schedules": [...]}; queries config.reports for all reports (row_id, report_name, is_active, report_url) and a second query joining config.reports to config.reports_jobs, jobs.jobs (occurance, occurs_at) and config.mail_groups (recipients where mail_config_id=1 and is_active) to expose each report's schedule; returns 500 with empty lists on error.

Returns JSON {"reports": [...]} listing the report definition files (sorted filenames matching rpt_*.json) found in the REPORTS_DIR directory via the _reports_list() helper; returns an empty list if the directory does not exist.

Returns the 200 most recent retention-purge runs from log.retention_executions (newest first): executed_at, policy, target_table, cutoff_date, rows_deleted, purge_mode, regulation, success, error_message and sha256_manifest - the audit trail (with tamper-evident manifest hash) of what each purge deleted.

Returns all data-retention policies from config.retention_policies (ordered by id): target schema/table, retention_days, min_retain_days, timestamp_column, purge_mode, regulation and last_run_at - the automated purge rules for compliance-driven data minimisation.

Creates a retention policy in config.retention_policies from JSON policy_name/target_table/retention_days (required) plus target_schema (default log), min_retain_days (default 0), timestamp_column (default event_time), purge_mode (default DELETE) and regulation; returns retention_id.

Updates a retention policy: patches any of policy_name/target_schema/target_table/retention_days/min_retain_days/timestamp_column/purge_mode/regulation/is_active on config.retention_policies for retention_id.

Returns the catalogue of configured user risk-level bands (row_id, risk_level label, is_active) from rootcause.risk_level, ordered by row_id. Populates risk-level reference lists and filters in the GRC UI.

Lists per-login behavioural risk profiles from monitoring.user_risk_profiles, filtered to risk_score >= min_risk_score with optional case-insensitive server_name / login_name search. Each entry returns the computed risk_score, consecutive_high_risk streak and behavioural baselines (avg queries/hour, avg duration, avg logical reads, typical tables and active-hours window) plus last_updated, ordered highest-risk first. Feeds the user-risk leaderboard.

Drill-down timeline for one login on one server: returns the 20 most recent risk-scoring events from monitoring.user_risk_events (event_time, risk_score, risk_factors), newest first, explaining why that user's risk score changed.

Returns the PII / sensitive-column inventory: unions confirmed columns from monitoring.sensitive_schema with monitoring.schema columns whose names match the PII regex (PII_PATTERNS) and are not yet confirmed. Includes summary stats (total, sensitive, enabled/disabled, server count) and the distinct server and database lists. Powers the sensitive-data classification screen.
Bulk version of the sensitivity toggle: iterates the items[] list, updating monitoring.schema.is_enabled or deleting monitoring.sensitive_schema rows as appropriate, and returns the count updated.

Runs PII auto-discovery: inserts into monitoring.sensitive_schema every enabled monitoring.schema column whose name matches the PII regex and is not already classified, then reports how many new sensitive columns were found and the new total.

Toggles one column's sensitivity flag: for source='schema' it sets is_enabled on monitoring.schema (by row_id); for source='sensitive' with is_enabled=false it removes the row from monitoring.sensitive_schema. Includes or excludes a single column from PII scope.

Aggregates FortiAnalyzer IPS dashboard data: computes summed stats (total/critical/high/medium/blocked/monitored counts) from siem.fortianalyzer_ips_events and pulls severity, timeline (last 7 days), types (15), blocked (15), sources (10), victims (10), http_attacks (20) and monitored (20) from the siem.v_ips_* views, returning them all as one JSON object; logs and returns 500 on error.

Generates the IPS report PDF via JSONReportGenerator from templates/rpt_ips_fortianalyzer_ips_report.json and returns it as a FileResponse download named IPS_Report_<timestamp>.pdf; raises 500 if the template is missing or generation fails.

Generates the IPS PDF/HTML report via JSONReportGenerator from templates/rpt_ips_fortianalyzer_ips_report.json and emails both files to the request's recipients (subject default 'IPS Report - dbdome') using SMTP settings read from config.mail_config; returns 400 if recipients missing, 500 if template or SMTP config absent, and logs the send.

Returns the current weekly IPS report schedule for report 'IPS Report - dbdome' by joining config.reports, config.reports_jobs, jobs.jobs, jobs.job_schedules and mail_group 'ips_weekly', yielding is_active, occurance, occurs_at (first 5 chars), day_of_week (isodow of next_run), next_run and recipients; returns {"is_active": false} when no schedule exists.

Saves the weekly IPS report schedule (day_of_week default 1, occurs_at default '06:00:00', is_active default true, recipients) by upserting config.reports ('IPS Report - dbdome'), jobs.jobs (weekly), config.reports_jobs, computing the next weekly run time and upserting jobs.job_schedules, and upserting the 'ips_weekly' config.mail_groups recipients; returns the computed next_run and logs the save, rolling back with 500 on error.
Returns all configured SoD rules from config.sod_rules (ordered by rule_id) - the toxic-combination definitions (conflicting role A vs role B patterns) that drive violation detection.

Creates a new SoD rule in config.sod_rules from JSON body rule_name (required), description, severity (default HIGH), regulation, role_a_patterns[] and role_b_patterns[]; returns the new rule_id. Defines a new conflicting-duties combination to monitor.

Updates an existing SoD rule: patches any supplied subset of rule_name, description, severity, regulation, role_a_patterns, role_b_patterns, is_active on config.sod_rules for rule_id. Used to tune a rule or enable/disable it (400 if the body has no updatable fields).

Lists Separation-of-Duties violations detected in the last 30 days from log.sod_violations (violation_id, detected_at, server, db_user, rule_name, severity, regulation, is_acknowledged), up to 500 newest-first - the SoD violation worklist.
Triages one SoD violation: sets is_acknowledged=TRUE and acknowledged_at=NOW() on log.sod_violations for the given violation_id, marking it as reviewed/accepted by an analyst.
Returns the active network block list from config.blocked_ips (is_active AND not expired), newest first: ip_address, reason, blocked_by, blocked_at and expires_at.

Blocks a client IP: upserts into config.blocked_ips (ON CONFLICT on ip_address re-activates the entry) with a reason and optional duration_mins TTL (NULL = permanent); ip_address is required. Then reloads the threat-response engine's in-memory entity cache so the block is enforced immediately.
Lifts an IP block by setting is_active=FALSE on config.blocked_ips for block_id, then reloads the threat-response entity cache so enforcement stops immediately.

Lists security incidents from log.security_incidents (up to 200), filtered by status (defaults to OPEN + ACKNOWLEDGED) and optional severity, ordered by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, ...) then newest-first. Each row carries title, severity, regulation, server/db_user/client_ip, description, status and timestamps - the incident queue.

Opens a new security incident in log.security_incidents from JSON body title (required), severity (default HIGH), regulation, server_name, db_user, client_ip, description and status (default OPEN); returns the new incident_id and writes an audit log line.

Updates an incident: patches any supplied subset of title/severity/regulation/server_name/db_user/client_ip/description/status on log.security_incidents, always bumping updated_at, and stamps resolved_at when status becomes RESOLVED. Used to triage or close an incident.

Returns all automated-response playbooks from config.threat_response_playbooks (ordered by id): the trigger (type/threshold/regulation), the response (type + params JSON), cooldown_mins and is_active - the SOAR-style automation rules.

Creates an automated-response playbook in config.threat_response_playbooks from JSON playbook_name, trigger_type and response_type (required), plus trigger_threshold (default 70), trigger_regulation, response_params (JSON object, default empty) and cooldown_mins (default 60); returns the new playbook_id.

Updates a playbook: patches any of playbook_name/description/trigger_type/trigger_threshold/trigger_regulation/response_type/cooldown_mins/is_active, and response_params (re-serialized to JSON), on config.threat_response_playbooks. Used to tune automation or enable/disable it.

Returns the 200 most recent automated-response actions from log.threat_response_log (newest first): triggered_at, playbook_name, trigger_type, subject, response_type, response_detail, success and error_message - the audit trail of what the automation actually executed.
Returns the active login-suspension list from config.suspended_users (is_active AND not expired), newest first: server_name, login_name, reason, suspended_by and timestamps.

Suspends a database login: upserts into config.suspended_users (ON CONFLICT on server_name+login_name re-activates) with a reason and optional duration_mins TTL; server_name and login_name are required. Reloads the threat-response entity cache to enforce immediately.
Ends a suspension by setting is_active=FALSE on config.suspended_users for suspension_id, then reloads the threat-response entity cache.
Returns the active TLS enforcement policies from config.tls_enforcement_policies (is_active), by server - the per-server require-SSL and minimum-TLS-version rules.

Creates a TLS enforcement policy in config.tls_enforcement_policies from JSON server_name (required) plus require_ssl (default true), action (default ALERT), min_tls_version and regulation (default PCI-DSS); returns tls_policy_id.
Updates a TLS policy: patches any of server_name/require_ssl/action/min_tls_version/regulation/is_active on config.tls_enforcement_policies for tls_policy_id.

Lists TLS/SSL enforcement violations from log.tls_violations in the last 24 hours (up to 500, newest first): server_name, db_user, client_ip, ssl_mode, risk_level, regulation and action_taken - connections that breached the encryption-in-transit policy.

Reads JSON body {report_id, is_active (default false)} and runs UPDATE config.reports SET is_active WHERE row_id=report_id, commits, and returns JSON {message, report_id, is_active}; returns 500 with the error message on failure.
Returns all rows from config.cve_watchlist (SELECT *) ordered by cve_id, casting cvss_score to float, as JSON {cves:[...]}, or 500 {error, cves:[]} on failure.

Upserts a CVE into config.cve_watchlist from the JSON body (requires cve_id; defaults severity='HIGH', affected_vendors=[], affected_versions=[]) using ON CONFLICT (cve_id) DO UPDATE of title, cvss_score, severity, affected_vendors, and affected_versions, then commits. Returns {message:'CVE saved'} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Updates config.cve_watchlist for the path cve_id, dynamically setting only supplied body keys (title, cvss_score, severity, affected_vendors, affected_versions, description); returns 400 if none supplied. Commits and returns {message:'CVE updated'} or 500 {detail} with rollback.

Lists up to 500 vulnerability findings from log.vulnerability_findings (finding_id, detected_at, server_name, vendor, db_version, cve_id, cvss_score, severity, patch_status, regulation), ordered by severity rank (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, else) then detected_at descending, with detected_at ISO-formatted and cvss_score cast to float. Returns {rows:[...]} or 500 {error, rows:[]}.

Starts an asynchronous vulnerability scan by launching run_vulnerability_scan from processes.vulnerability_scanner in a daemon background thread, returning immediately with {message:'Vulnerability scan started'} or 500 {detail} on failure.

Returns all rows from config.webook_alerts (row_id, metric_type, send_mail_alert, send_siem_alert, send_diagnosis_evidence) ordered by metric_type as JSON {channels}; on error returns a 500 with an empty channels list.

Renders an inline 'Send report by mail' HTML form for the named report, collecting recipients only (no DB work); the /capture_report variant posts to /submit-report_capture, the /generate_report variant posts to /submit-generate_report.

Serves static configuration screens by opening and returning a template: templates/email_configuration.html (/email_configuration), templates/retention_policy.html (/retention_policy), or templates/serverform.html (/serverform).

Handler reused for three GET routes: serves templates/custom_metrics.html (/custom_metrics_update) and redirects to Grafana dashboards for /email_configuration (configuration) and /take_action (take-action).
Restores a database from its backup (reverting all changes) via processes.rbac_provisioning.restore_database, then 302-redirects back.
Redirects (302) to the Grafana dbdome dashboard at http://<request-host>:3000/d/ad7kkx7/dbdome; logs the request, no DB work.

Generates a report PDF: reads SMTP settings from config.mail_config and the report query from config.reports, runs it via fetch_data_report_once, writes reports/<name>_<timestamp>.pdf via export_to_pdf_once, then 302-redirects back to the referer.
Irreversibly anonymizes a column (or all big character columns when column omitted) via processes.data_protection.anonymize (audited), then 302-redirects back.
Staged anonymization phase 2: switches the live table with its latest pre-copy via processes.data_protection.anonymize_actual, then 302-redirects back.
Staged anonymization phase 3: creates the backup schema (default dbdome_backup) and archives the original dated copy into it via processes.data_protection.anonymize_confirm, then 302-redirects back.
Staged anonymization phase 1: copies the table to <table>_<datetime> and anonymizes the copy via processes.data_protection.anonymize_pre (original untouched), then 302-redirects back.
Read-only preview: runs SELECT TOP <rows> on the latest anonymized dry-run copy via processes.data_protection.preview_copy and renders the rows as an HTML table.
Applies SQL Server Dynamic Data Masking on a column via processes.data_protection.apply_dynamic_mask (audited in metrics.dp_log), then 302-redirects back to the referring dashboard.
Reverts Dynamic Data Masking on a column (DROP MASKED) via processes.data_protection.revert_dynamic_mask (audited), then 302-redirects back.

Renders an inline HTML form: the /addrecipients variant shows a recipient-group form (POST /submit-addrecipients); the /mailconfiguration variant shows an SMTP mail-config form, prefilling smtp_* fields and recipients from config.mail_config and config.mail_groups (password via decrypt_secret) when row_id is supplied.

Handles POST /submit-alert-rule: takes issue_id and event_rule_id (required) plus rootcause_number and optional row_id, and inserts or updates a row in config.alerts_issue_root_causes. Returns a JSON confirmation or 500 error.

Handles POST /submit-alert-threshold: takes alert_id (required) plus level, value_start, value_end and optional row_id, and either updates the existing config.thresholds row linked through config.alerts_thresholds (when row_id is given) or inserts a new threshold and links it to the alert. Returns a JSON confirmation or 500 error.

Handler report_capture, bound to POST /submit-generate_report and POST /submit-report_capture. For /submit-generate_report it takes report, recipients and referer, looks up the report_url in config.reports, generates PDF+HTML via JSONReportGenerator, reads SMTP settings from config.mail_config and emails the report. For /submit-report_capture it takes report, url, recipients and referer and calls capture_grafana_dashboard_pdf(url, report, recipients) to capture and email a Grafana dashboard PDF. Both redirect to the referer (or a fallback Grafana dashboard).

Handles POST /submit-global-param: takes key (required) and value, and upserts that key/value into config.global_params (updates if the key exists, otherwise inserts). Returns a JSON confirmation or 500 error.

Handles POST /submit-mailconfiguration: accepts SMTP form fields (smtp_server, smtp_user, smtp_password, smtp_port, tls, smtp_sender required; optional row_id, group_name, recipients, group_id) and upserts the mail server config via CALL config.save_mail_config with the password encrypted through encrypt_secret; if recipients is supplied it also upserts the linked recipient group via config.save_mail_group. Redirects to the referer (or the Grafana configuration dashboard) on completion.

Handles POST /submit-processform: takes process_name, interval and active (all required) and activates/updates a scheduled process via CALL metrics.process_activate. Redirects to the Grafana processes dashboard.

Handles POST /submit-report-schedule: takes optional report_id (or 'new'), report_name, schedule, occurs_at, recipients, report_type, report_query, report_url and is_active, and creates or updates a scheduled report by inserting/updating config.reports, finding/creating a jobs.jobs schedule, linking via config.reports_jobs, seeding jobs.job_schedules, and optionally adding a config.mail_groups recipient group. Returns JSON with the report_id or an error; report_name is required when creating a new report.

Handler report_capture, bound to POST /submit-generate_report and POST /submit-report_capture. For /submit-generate_report it takes report, recipients and referer, looks up the report_url in config.reports, generates PDF+HTML via JSONReportGenerator, reads SMTP settings from config.mail_config and emails the report. For /submit-report_capture it takes report, url, recipients and referer and calls capture_grafana_dashboard_pdf(url, report, recipients) to capture and email a Grafana dashboard PDF. Both redirect to the referer (or a fallback Grafana dashboard).

Handles POST /submit-reportbymail: takes server, start_time, end_time, recipients, reportname and referer (all required), reads SMTP settings from config.mail_config and the report_query from config.reports, runs the query for the time range, generates a timestamped PDF, emails it to the recipients as an attachment, then deletes the temp PDF. Redirects to the referer or the Grafana transaction-report dashboard.

Handles POST /submit-risklevel: takes referer and a comma-separated row_ids plus per-row active_{id} flags, and updates rootcause.risk_level.is_active for each listed row_id in one transaction. Returns 400 if row_ids is missing, redirects to the referer on success, otherwise returns JSON {ok:true}.

Handles POST /submit-serverform: takes server, add_delete_modify, ipAddress, port, dbVendor and authType (required) plus optional dbVersion, user, password and service_name, and adds/modifies/deletes a monitored server via CALL metrics.upsert_monitored_server; also writes the submitted data to server_data.json. Redirects to the Grafana automation-and-workflows dashboard.

Handles POST /submit-webhook-alert: takes metric_type (required) plus send_mail_alert, send_siem_alert, send_diagnosis_evidence boolean-string flags and optional row_id, and inserts or updates the alert channel row in config.webook_alerts. Returns a JSON confirmation or 500 error.
Handles POST /submit_custom_metric_enable: takes a required row_id and toggles/enables that custom metric via CALL gapi.custom_metric_enable. Redirects to the Grafana configuration dashboard.

Handles POST /submit_custom_metrics (handler submit_custom_metrics): takes metric_name, metric_desc, query, db_vendor_selector and action_select (all required) and upserts a custom metric definition via CALL gapi.custom_metrics_upsert. Redirects to the Grafana configuration dashboard.

Handles POST /submit_custom_metrics (handler show_custom_metrics, line 2750): takes process_name, interval and active (all required) and calls CALL metrics.process_activate to activate/update the process. Redirects to the Grafana processes dashboard.

Handles POST /submit_custom_metrics_update: takes a row_id parameter, opens a DB connection/engine but performs no write, and just redirects to the Grafana configuration dashboard (no-op redirect stub).

Handles POST /submit_email_configuration: takes smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_password and tls (all required) and upserts the email configuration via CALL gapi.email_configuration_upsert (password stored as-is, not encrypted). Redirects to the Grafana email-configuration dashboard.

Handler submit_metrics_enable, bound to POST /submit_metrics_enable and POST /submit_metrics_enable_all_servers: takes required action_select (enable flag) and row_id and calls CALL gapi.metric_enable (single server) or CALL gapi.metric_enable_all_servers (all servers) respectively. Redirects to the Grafana configuration dashboard.

Handles POST /submit_metrics_enable (handler show_metrics_enable, line 2791): takes process_name, interval and active (all required) and calls CALL metrics.process_activate. Redirects to the Grafana processes dashboard.

Handler submit_metrics_enable, bound to POST /submit_metrics_enable and POST /submit_metrics_enable_all_servers: takes required action_select (enable flag) and row_id and calls CALL gapi.metric_enable (single server) or CALL gapi.metric_enable_all_servers (all servers) respectively. Redirects to the Grafana configuration dashboard.

Handler reused for three GET routes: serves templates/custom_metrics.html (/custom_metrics_update) and redirects to Grafana dashboards for /email_configuration (configuration) and /take_action (take-action).

Handles POST /submit_retention_policy (handler show_submit_retention_policy, line 2832): takes process_name, interval and active (all required) and calls CALL metrics.process_activate. Redirects to the Grafana processes dashboard.

Handles POST /submit_siem_configuration: takes select_vendor, url and secret (all required) and upserts the SIEM interface configuration (vendor name, URL, app key) via CALL metrics.siem_upsert. Redirects to the Grafana siem-configuration dashboard.

Handler reused for three GET routes: serves templates/custom_metrics.html (/custom_metrics_update) and redirects to Grafana dashboards for /email_configuration (configuration) and /take_action (take-action).

Handles POST /test-connection: takes ipAddress and dbVendor (required) plus optional port, authType, user, password and service_name, and attempts a live test connection to the target database (MSSQL via pyodbc, Oracle, PostgreSQL via psycopg2, or MySQL/MariaDB via pymysql) running a version query. Returns JSON {success, message} with the server version or the error; makes no config changes.

Calls the monitoring.sensitive_schema_column_enable procedure for the schema_column query param to activate a sensitive schema column, then redirects to Grafana (sender path or the email-configuration dashboard).
Serves the webhook alerts screen (renders templates/webhook_alerts.html).
Toggles a config.webook_alerts flag by calling config.set_webook_alert(row_id, field, value), then 302-redirects back to the referring Grafana dashboard (default webhook-alerts-config).
